title: Harvest Runway - Onboarding Ops & VPC Kickoff
next_steps: Redwood to share security packet + SOC2/ISO docs (Jordan)
SE deep-dive on VPC network and KMS integration next week (Sam)
Provision trial Dedicated cluster for benchmark (Priya)
Customer to provide sample prompt set and latency targets (Marta)
action_items: Jordan Lee: Send security pack + SOC2 evidence by 2026-02-10
Sam Ortega: Run initial network diagram and VPC peering checklist by 2026-02-12
Marta Valdez: Share sample prompt set and expected qps by 2026-02-11
Noah Kim: Provide egress/ingress firewall rules & proxy constraints by 2026-02-10
header: Date: 2026-02-07; Start: 15:00 PST; Duration: ~52 mins; Purpose: Implementation kickoff for Harvest Runway onboarding to Redwood Private/Dedicated; Attendees: see metadata.
summary: Initial implementation kickoff: agreement on pilot scope (private VPC deployment with KMS integration), high-level runbook, SLA targets (90ms p50 target for customer-facing prompts), security documentation request, and scheduling of an SE-led technical deep dive. Customer expressed constraints around egress rules, corporate proxy, and data retention requirements; Redwood outlined fallback to hosted API for early dev and Dedicated cluster for production. Agreed to provision trial Dedicated capacity for benchmark and share security pack.
topics: 1) Pilot scope and success criteria; 2) Deployment model options (Private vs Dedicated vs Hosted); 3) Network & KMS integration constraints; 4) Security/compliance asks (SOC2, audit logs, SSO); 5) Performance targets and benchmarking; 6) Next steps and owners.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll do a quick intros then jump into the onboarding scope. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood. With me are Priya and Sam from CS and SE.
[00:12] Marta Valdez: Hi all, Marta here. Head of ML at Harvest Runway. We're excited to get rolling.
[00:18] Noah Kim: Noah, infra lead — I'll own the VPC bits.
[00:22] Sam Ortega: Hey, Sam SE. I'll take the technical deep dive.
[00:26] Priya Nair: Priya, CSM — I'll be your day-to-day for the pilot.
[00:33] Jordan Lee: Cool. Quick agenda: confirm pilot goals, deployment model (you'd indicated Private deployment), network constraints, security asks, and next steps.
[00:44] Marta Valdez: Yes Private is the preference — we have sensitive PII-ish inference requests and need strict residency. But we also want a fast dev loop, so we may need hosted foo for early dev.
[00:56] Jordan Lee: Totally — that's a common pattern. We'll outline a hybrid: hosted for dev, then Dedicated or Private (VPC) for production. Priya: any notes on Dedicated burst vs Private?
[01:08] Priya Nair: Sure, Dedicated can give you reserved capacity with isolation; Private gives you a customer-managed VPC and control plane. There's a bit more setup for Private (peering, KMS integration) but it meets strict compliance needs.
[01:23] Noah Kim: For us, the blocker is egress. We run through a corporate proxy and we have strict outbound rules — can Redwood work with an outbound-only NAT and proxy TLS inspection?
[01:36] Sam Ortega: Yes, we've done setups with corporate proxies, but we need to validate certificate pinning and SNI behaviors. We'll share a VPC checklist. A note: KMS integration requires either a cross-account IAM role or a customer-managed key handshake — what KMS are you using?
[01:52] Sana Ahmed: We're on AWS KMS, CMKs managed by our security team. We need key usage audit logs and to know if any tokens ever leave the VPC.
[02:03] Jordan Lee: Short answer: your keys stay in your account; Redwood supports customer-managed KMS via an IAM role and we're able to store audit logs. We'll pack the security docs with exact flow diagrams.
[02:14] Carlos Rivera: From data ingestion side, we plan to send customer prompts with hashed identifiers, but we need to understand retention windows and any caching of prompts or KV cache in the runtime.
[02:26] Sam Ortega: Good question. Runtime does prefix/KV caching for performance; for Private deployments we can configure cache eviction to zero retention if required. For Hosted, there are default caches but we can opt out. Also quantization/stateful caches — sometimes transcripts show 'KV cash' in logs (laughs).
[02:45] Marta Valdez: Haha, yes please opt-out for PII flows.
[02:48] Jordan Lee: Noted. On performance: what latency targets do you have and expected qps?
[02:54] Marta Valdez: For the customer-facing assistant, p50 under 120ms and p95 under 300ms for 2k qps during peak. For batch analytics embeddings it's less strict.
[03:05] Sam Ortega: 2k qps with sub-300ms p95 is ambitious — depends on model size and sequence length. We'll recommend model variants and quantization profiles. For Dedicated we can reserve GPUs and tune batching to meet those SLOs. We'll run a benchmark with your prompt set.
[03:22] Noah Kim: What's the expected infra footprint for that? GPUs? Autoscaling?
[03:26] Sam Ortega: We'll propose a starter config — likely A100-ish type or large L40-class, and autoscale policies with burst capacity. But exact instance count after benchmarks.
[03:37] Sana Ahmed: Security: SOC2 is table-stakes. We also need SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, SIEM integration (splunk). Can we get syslog or cloudwatch forwarding?
[03:49] Priya Nair: Yes — for Private we support audit log streaming to your cloud logging; SAML is supported for console access, and we have RBAC mapped to roles. We'll include a runbook for SSO mapping.
[04:02] Leah Turner: On the product side, we need rollback policies for model updates, canary deploys, and automatic fallback if a big model is slower.
[04:11] Sam Ortega: Redwood's rollouts support canary and A/B plus automatic fallback to a cheaper/fast variant. We'll show the Console demo in the SE deep dive.
[04:20] Marta Valdez: Great. Anything else on compliance like data residency or contractual needs?
[04:25] Jordan Lee: We'll include the compliance pack. For contractual SLAs we can include latency/uptime terms in Dedicated contracts. Priya will loop in Sales on the procurement path.
[04:36] Marta Valdez: Timeline: we want a pilot running in 3 weeks if possible — initial dev environment first week, VPC peering + KMS second, benchmark third. Feasible?
[04:45] Jordan Lee: Aggressive but doable. We'll provision a Dedicated trial within 5 business days and start the peering checklist. Sam: any blockers?
[04:52] Sam Ortega: The main blockers will be firewall/proxy configs and KMS role setup. If Noah can get us the egress rules and the account IDs we can preflight.
[05:02] Noah Kim: I'll share the firewall rules and proxy vendor; we use BlueShield proxy and have TLS inspection.
[05:09] Sana Ahmed: Also, we need an encryption attestation for at-rest keys and whether Redwood ever stores unencrypted token payloads.
[05:18] Jordan Lee: Keys remain customer-managed; Redwood stores data encrypted at rest. We do not retain unencrypted payloads; default retention is 7 days for logs, but for Private you can set retention to zero. We'll confirm in the security doc.
[05:31] Carlos Rivera: About the SDKs: we use a node/python stack; do you have code samples for streaming and function-calling?
[05:38] Sam Ortega: Yes we have SDKs and streaming examples. We'll share a short repo link in the follow-up. Note the streaming API has a small reconnection pattern to handle network proxies.
[05:48] Marta Valdez: Nice. Also curious about cost: we need a rough estimate for 2k qps and embeddings usage.
[05:55] Jordan Lee: We'll send an initial cost model — ballpark for Dedicated reserve + network egress you'll see per-token compute and infra amortized. Priya will attach a spreadsheet.
[06:07] Priya Nair: I'll put together a pilot cost sheet and sample invoices.
[06:12] Jordan Lee: Ok let's recap next steps: we'll share security packet + SOC2 docs, SE will run the VPC preflight checklist and schedule deep dive next Tue, we provision Dedicated trial, customer shares prompt set and firewall details.
[06:25] Marta Valdez: Sounds good. One last question — can we run small A/B of model variants during pilot to validate fallbacks?
[06:33] Sam Ortega: Absolutely — rollouts are supported; we can set traffic weights and automatic fallback to a smaller model if latency rises above threshold.
[06:41] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Thanks everyone, we'll send the notes and the links. Meeting adjourned.
[06:47] (end)
